A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Scone method and SconeEval benchmark. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary material are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on OmniContext and SconeEval, training ablations, threshold sensitivity, qualitative analyses, and a human evaluation.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds a bridge-focused human evaluation and qualitative comparison.

M1.justification: The BAGEL-based architecture, MSE objective, two-stage training, and semantic attention mask remain unchanged. The layer-8 mask applied to layers 9–15 is documented in both appendices. Consolidating the equations does not alter the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training sources, OmniContext, and the 409-case SconeEval benchmark with the same character, object, scene, composition, and distinction coverage. The added bridge analyses reuse these existing scenarios.

E2.justification: v2 adds a human comparison between Echo-4o, Scone without the bridge, and Scone with the bridge. The comparator sets in Tables 2–3 and the original OmniGen2/UniWorld-V2/Scone user study remain unchanged. VSM and AlphaCLIP are discussed but not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: The additional user study introduces a controlled human comparison of bridge variants using the existing evaluation procedure. Original resolution, training budgets, and scoring aggregation remain unchanged. Section 4.3 also omits v1's description of F1 as an average of precision and recall, without establishing a changed computation.

E4.justification: New Figure 9 illustrates subject errors, redundancy, and blending with versus without the bridge; an additional user study tests human preference for these variants. Existing training ablations, layer analyses, and failure examples remain. The threshold study is relocated from Appendix D to Section 5.4, not newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions report three sampling rounds with three scoring rounds each, averaging nine result groups, and retain Figure 8's standard-deviation analysis. The added user study introduces no new uncertainty estimates, significance tests, or repeated-run reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds preference scores of 0.27 for Echo-4o, 0.31 for Scone without the bridge, and 0.42 with the bridge, plus Figure 9's qualitative findings. Tables 2–6 and the original user-study scores are unchanged; the new preferences are from a separate comparison.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 combines five equation displays into three while preserving the normalization, cosine similarity, relevance averaging, and attention-mask definitions. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain Scone, the understanding bridge, and SconeEval, with the same claims about composition and distinction performance. The introduction's emphasis on internal understanding largely restates v1's discussion of the unified architecture rather than introducing a new contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly motivates GPT-4.1 evaluation by contrasting it with mask-requiring VSM and AlphaCLIP. v1's explicit assertion of empirically faster processing is omitted, although general efficiency arguments remain. The unrealistic-interaction limitation and token-efficiency future direction are retained.

D1.justification: Training-data quantities, filtering rules, construction prompts, training stages, and layer choices are retained, sometimes condensed or relocated. The model, benchmark, and training-data access statement is unchanged. No substantive new implementation recipe or reproducibility settings are supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Mind-the-glitch, AlphaCLIP, and Expand and Prune, and removes the Seedream 4.0 reference. The new metric discussion modestly expands positioning, while the main relationship to subject-driven generation and unified models remains stable.

P1.justification: The paper substantially condenses and rewrites benchmark, experiment, and appendix prose. Quantitative and qualitative sections are merged, the separate Discussion is absorbed elsewhere, threshold analysis moves into the main text, and future work moves to the limitations appendix. Affiliations and acknowledgments are also updated.

P2.justification: The evaluation layout is substantially reorganized: Tables 2–3 are colocated, Figures 6–7 are separated, and ablation and threshold tables are grouped together. Figure 9 is added, Table 6 moves from the appendix, and supplementary displays are redistributed with revised captions. Most underlying figures and all existing numerical tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v1 supports the bridge mainly through automatic-score ablations; v2 adds human preference evidence and concrete failure comparisons in Figure 9, modestly strengthening that support. The reorganized presentation makes the analyses easier to locate. Gains are limited because the main results remain unchanged, and Figure 3 retains stale equation references after renumbering.
